index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the general DAB (Detection-Aware Bandit) procedure, structured into two main sections: an upper schematic block diagram and a lower temporal timeline. The global layout is divided horizontally, with the top half depicting the algorithmic components and their interactions, and the bottom half showing the dynamic behavior over time.

In the upper section, three primary modules are presented. On the left, 'Forced Exploration' is labeled with the purpose '...to bypass focusing on optimal actions'. This module is represented as plain black text without a bounding box. Centrally, two rounded rectangular boxes with a muted teal fill represent core algorithmic components. The top box is labeled 'Change Detector (D)' with a subtext stating '...with guaranteed probabilities of false alarm and delayed detection'. Below it is 'Stationary Bandit (B)', with the subtext '..used as is'. A curved arrow originates from the Forced Exploration label and points to the Change Detector, indicating its role in influencing or feeding into the detector. A straight downward arrow connects the Change Detector to the Stationary Bandit, annotated with '...triggers restart', signifying that a detected change initiates a reset of the bandit. Finally, a rightward arrow extends from the Stationary Bandit to the label 'Arm to be pulled', indicating the output decision of which action to select.

The lower section displays a horizontal timeline labeled 'Time' along the x-axis. Three distinct traces are shown. The top trace, labeled 'Environment', is a horizontal line that remains constant until a vertical dashed line marks 'Change occurs', after which it steps upward, indicating a shift in the environment's state. Below this, a series of light gray rectangular blocks represent discrete rounds or time intervals; these are spaced irregularly, with some clustered together. A dotted vertical line aligns with the 'Change occurs' event and is labeled 'Triggers restart'. From this point, several arrows point from the timeline to a cluster of blocks, accompanied by the annotation 'Rounds dedicated to forced exploration', illustrating that after a change is detected, specific rounds are allocated for exploration. The bottom trace is a smooth, purple curve labeled 'Learning settles down', which decreases over time, representing convergence of learning. At the point of the environmental change, this curve experiences a sharp upward jump before resuming its decline, reflecting the disruption and subsequent re-learning phase triggered by the restart.
